thought_title: Hoisted by the cross, roped by the Spirit

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Ἔγνων δὲ παροδεύσαντάς τινας ἐκεῖθεν, ἔχοντας κακὴν διδαχήν: οὓς οὐκ εἰάσατε σπεῖραι εἰς ὑμᾶς, βύσαντες τὰ ὦτα, εἰς τὸ μὴ παραδέξασθαι τὰ σπειρόμενα ὑπ’ αὐτῶν, ὡς ὄντες λίθοι ναοῦ πατρός, ἡτοιμασμένοι εἰς οἰκοδομὴν θεοῦ πατρός, ἀναφερόμενοι εἰς τὰ ὕψη διὰ τῆς μηχανῆς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν σταυρός, σχοινίῳ χρώμενοι τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ: ἡ δὲ πίστις ὑμῶν ἀναγωγεὺς ὑμῶν, ἡ δὲ ἀγάπη ὁδὸς ἡ ἀναφέρουσα εἰς θεόν. [2] ἐστὲ οὖν καὶ σύνοδοι πάντες, θεοφόροι καὶ ναοφόροι, χριστοφόροι, ἁγιοφόροι, κατὰ πάντα κεκοσμημένοι ἐντολαῖς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ: οἶς καὶ ἀγαλλιώμενος ἠξιώθην δἰ ὦν γράφω προσομιλῆσαι ὑμῖν καὶ συγχαρῆναι, ὅτι κατ’ ἀνθρώπων βίον οὐδὲν ἀγαπᾶτε εἰ μὴ μόνον τὸν θεόν.
pass_a_gloss: But I have learned that certain people passed through from there who had bad teaching. You did not allow them to sow it among you; you stopped your ears so as not to receive the things being sown by them, because you are stones of the Father's temple, prepared for the building of God the Father, carried up to the heights by the hoisting engine of Jesus Christ, which is the cross, using the Holy Spirit as the rope. Your faith is what draws you up, and love is the road that leads up to God. So you are all fellow travelers in procession, God-bearers and temple-bearers, Christ-bearers, bearers of holy things, adorned in every respect with the commandments of Jesus Christ. Rejoicing in these things, I have been counted worthy, through the things I am writing, to converse with you and to rejoice with you, because in your human life you love nothing except God alone.

lemmas.gloss: that which hauls up; hoist, windlass
fellow traveler, companion on the road (as in a religious procession)

pass_b_english: I have heard that some people passed your way from there, carrying bad teaching. You would not let them sow it among you. You stopped your ears so as not to take in what they were sowing. For you are stones of the Father's temple, made ready for the building of God the Father (1 Corinthians 3:9). You are lifted to the heights by the crane of Jesus Christ, which is the cross, and you use the Holy Spirit as your rope. Your faith is the winch that raises you, and love is the road that climbs to God.

So you are all companions in one procession: God-bearers and temple-bearers, Christ-bearers, bearers of holy things, dressed at every point in the commandments of Jesus Christ. Rejoicing in all this, I have been counted worthy to talk with you through what I write and to share your joy, because in this human life you love nothing but God alone.

choices.term: διὰ τῆς μηχανῆς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ... σχοινίῳ ... ἀναγωγεύς
choices.english: the crane of Jesus Christ ... the rope ... the winch
choices.why: Ignatius builds a construction-site picture: stones hauled up by a crane (the cross), a cable (the Spirit), and a hoist (faith). Plain machine words keep the image concrete.

choices.english: you are all companions in one procession
choices.why: σύνοδοι are fellow travelers; the -φόροι words that follow picture worshipers carrying sacred objects in a festival procession.
rejected: you, as well as all your fellow-travellers (ANF; misreads the predicate)

choices.english: God-bearers and temple-bearers, Christ-bearers, bearers of holy things
choices.why: Keeps Ignatius's coined chain intact; each word stays a bearer-compound.
rejected: full of God (loses the processional carrying)

choices.why: The phrase qualifies their present human existence, not a 'Christian life'.
rejected: with respect to your Christian life (ANF; not in the Greek)

anf_compare.notes: Overall sense aligned, but ANF 'You, therefore, as well as all your fellow-travellers' misreads ἐστὲ οὖν καὶ σύνοδοι πάντες, which says the readers themselves are all fellow travelers. ANF 'with respect to your Christian life' is not in the Greek κατ’ ἀνθρώπων βίον ('in human life'). Lake's 'οἷς καὶ ἀγαλλιώμενος ἠξιώθην' differs from Lightfoot's ὅθεν καὶ ἀγαλλιῶμαι ὅτι ἠξιώθην; ANF's 'in whom also I exult' follows neither exactly.

bible_refs.note: θεοῦ οἰκοδομή: God's building; Ignatius has οἰκοδομὴν θεοῦ πατρός

notes: Whole chapter 9 (sections 1-2) matches the ANF span.
Possible echoes kept out of the reading text: 1 Peter 2:5 (living stones), Ephesians 2:20-22 (holy temple), John 12:32 (lifted up, drawn to me).
Lake's accentuation here shows copy artifacts (οἶς for οἷς, δἰ ὦν for δι’ ὧν); the Greek is reproduced exactly as supplied.

review.notes: p1 checked clause by clause. Ἔγνων δὲ παροδεύσαντάς τινας ἐκεῖθεν, ἔχοντας κακὴν διδαχήν matches A learned/passed through/had bad teaching and B heard/passed your way/carrying bad teaching as the same report. οὐκ εἰάσατε σπεῖραι εἰς ὑμᾶς, βύσαντες τὰ ὦτα, εἰς τὸ μὴ παραδέξασθαι τὰ σπειρόμενα ὑπ’ αὐτῶν keeps the refusal and purpose-negation in both. ὡς ὄντες λίθοι ναοῦ πατρός, ἡτοιμασμένοι εἰς οἰκοδομὴν θεοῦ πατρός is stones prepared for God the Father's building; B's (1 Corinthians 3:9) matches the supplied wording note θεοῦ οἰκοδομή / οἰκοδομὴν θεοῦ πατρός. ἀναφερόμενοι εἰς τὰ ὕψη διὰ τῆς μηχανῆς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν σταυρός, σχοινίῳ χρώμενοι τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ keeps passive lift by the cross-machine and the Ephesians using the Spirit as rope. ἡ δὲ πίστις ὑμῶν ἀναγωγεὺς ὑμῶν, ἡ δὲ ἀγάπη ὁδὸς ἡ ἀναφέρουσα εἰς θεόν is faith the haul/winch and love the upward road. ἐστὲ οὖν καὶ σύνοδοι πάντες, θεοφόροι καὶ ναοφόροι, χριστοφόροι, ἁγιοφόροι, κατὰ πάντα κεκοσμημένοι ἐντολαῖς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ and ὅτι κατ’ ἀνθρώπων βίον οὐδὲν ἀγαπᾶτε εἰ μὴ μόνον τὸν θεόν are intact, including nothing-except-God-alone. Accent artifacts οἶς/δἰ ὦν are disclosed and read as οἷς/δι’ ὧν. Title names the hoist-and-rope thought.

Source identity: Locked Greek matches Ignatius' Epistle to the Ephesians 9:1-2 per supplied file locus and edition. Completeness: Both paragraphs fully rendered; no omissions of clauses, qualifications, or repetitions. Negation: Greek οὓς οὐκ εἰάσατε σπεῖραι εἰς ὑμᾶς correctly rendered as 'You did not allow them to sow it among you' (Pass A) and 'You would not let them sow it among you' (Pass B). Agency: Subjects and verbs align—Ignatius as learner, Ephesians as actors stopping ears, etc. Modality: Causal clauses (ὡς ὄντες..., ἀναφερόμενοι..., ὅς...) preserved via participles and relative clauses in both Pass A and B. Doctrine: Architectural metaphor (stones, temple, hoisting engine, rope, winch, road) consistently conveyed; no doctrinal distortion. Scripture: Inline citation (1 Corinthians 3:9) correctly added per bible_refs and notes; matches Ignatius' allusion to God's building. Title: 'Hoisted by the cross, roped by the Spirit' names the thought (mechanism of ascent via cross and Spirit), not just locus. Notes disclose OCR artifacts (οἶς for οἷς, δἰ ὦν for δι’ ὧN) as required. All checks satisfied.
